description: NFS shares mounted into a consumer guest (ADR-029): a TAPPaaS export on a cluster node, a share on a registered, unmanaged server, or an unmodelled server's path.
_note: The consumer's side only. The node's own exports are the module-tier `nfs` object (pvehost/fields.json), converged by pvehost/update.sh; this service checks a consumer's mounts against them (the two-key check), has the node build a declared export it names (D11), and writes the mounts into the guest. The `nfs` object's DEFINITION lives in the module tier (pvehost/fields.json) because registered NFS servers carry it too; its change semantics are here, with the service that converges it, as backup:filesystem does for `backup`.

nfs.changeNote: Converged by the node's own update (pvehost/update.sh → nfs_node_reconcile): exports are created, re-quota'd, re-granted and unshared live; nothing reboots. name, pool and an allocated owner are immutable in substance — a rename or a pool move is a data migration and is not attempted; the reconcile treats the old dataset as an orphan and keeps it.

mounts.description: The NFS shares this guest mounts (ADR-029 v0.8 D3). Each entry: {path, share, subdir?, access?, required?, stopUnits?, stopCommand?, startCommand?}. share is a Site-unique share NAME — never the machine that carries it; it is reached through its DNS alias nfs-<share>.mgmt.internal — or <ip-or-host>:/<path> for an unmodelled server. A share no server declares leaves the mount pending: the directory stays local, and is migrated into once the share appears (with consent).

path.description: Absolute directory in the guest. Not /, /etc, /nix, /var, /usr, /boot or a system path.

share.description: A Site-unique share name (reached through nfs-<share>.mgmt.internal, ADR-029 D2b), or <ip-or-host>:/<path> for an unmodelled server. The <instance>:<name> form of v0.1–v0.7 is withdrawn.

subdir.description: A directory inside the share to mount instead of its root (ADR-029 D15). Relative, no . or ..; created on first use, owned by the share's owner. Organisation, not isolation: the grant is per share.

access.description: What the consumer asks for. Must not exceed the export's grant.

required.description: false: nofail + automount — the guest boots and the app starts without the share. true: the mount is required at boot.

stopUnits.description: systemd units in the guest to stop while the directory is migrated into its share, and start again after (ADR-029 D14). An open-files guard aborts the migration if anything else still holds the directory.

stopCommand.description: A command run in the guest (sudo) before stopUnits stop, for what is not a systemd unit (ADR-029 D14).

startCommand.description: A command run in the guest (sudo) after stopUnits start again (ADR-029 D14).

mounts.changeNote: The mounts are reconciled whole: update-service.sh rewrites the guest's generated mount list (NixOS fragment, applied by the rebuild the update runs; Debian fstab block, applied at once). Changing share or subdir remounts and moves no data; only a pending mount whose share has appeared is migrated into, and only with consent (rebootOk or --allow-disruption) — that is the one change that stops the app. Nothing reboots.
